outcomes.description: Transform the image into a pencil drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

nodes.question: Does the image show the original visual content rendered in a pencil-drawn style?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image visibly represents its content as a pencil drawing; fail if there is sufficient evidence that no pencil-drawing transformation has occurred; unknown if the image or its style cannot be assessed reliably. Partial evidence of a pencil-drawn style is progress, not completion.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied image with the requested transformation: assess whether its visual content is rendered in a pencil-drawn style. Do not require a particular pencil technique.

nodes.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

nodes.question: Does the image visibly appear as a completed pencil drawing?
nodes.criteria: Compose both supports under R1 without treating either support as completion credit by itself. Complete (yes) only when s1 passes. Partial only when s1 does not pass, s2 passes, and the evidence is sufficient to establish some requested progress without complete fulfillment. Absent (no) only when s1 fails and s2 fails, with sufficient evidence that no requested change has progressed. Unknown when required evidence is unresolved, including when s1 is unknown and completion cannot be established, or when s2 is unknown and absence or partial progress cannot be established. Unrelated edits never count as progress.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

transaction.reason: The existing checks establish visible sketch-like progress but do not distinguish that from a substantially completed pencil drawing. Add a nested, image-grounded check for the extent and consistency of the style conversion; revise the readout so progress alone supports partial, not completion. The added check uses the broad progress observation as context, not as independent confirmation.

actions.question: Does the pencil-drawing treatment substantially and consistently render the image's visual content as a drawing, rather than merely applying a pale or grainy sketch-like effect while retaining a predominantly photographic appearance?
actions.criteria: Pass only if comparison of source and edit shows that the requested pencil-drawing style is substantially realized across the image's salient content, with drawing-like rendering rather than merely a partial or superficial effect. Fail if there is sufficient visual evidence that the treatment falls short of substantial conversion. Unknown if the extent or consistency cannot be assessed reliably. A pass on the ancestor establishes only progress and is not itself evidence of substantial completion.
actions.binding: Inspect the source and edited images directly. Use the ancestor's progress observation as context, then independently assess the extent and consistency of the style transformation across the meal and surrounding scene. Do not treat muted color, grain, or isolated sketch-like details alone as proof of completion.

actions.criteria: Compose all three supports without treating correlated observations as independent proof. Complete (yes) only when s3 passes, establishing substantial and consistent conversion. Partial only when s1 or s2 establishes visible requested progress and s3 fails, establishing that the transformation falls short of substantial completion. Absent (no) only when s1 and s2 both fail with sufficient evidence of no requested progress. Unknown when evidence needed to distinguish these states is unresolved; in particular, a pass on s1 or s2 alone cannot establish completion, and an unknown s3 prevents deciding between complete and partial. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The program adds an unjustified completion constraint: s3 requires drawing-like marks, tonal structure, and reduced photographic appearance across salient content, and rejects a pencil-like filter. The instruction asks for a pencil drawing but does not exclude filters or prescribe those techniques. The fulfillment rule then makes s3 the sole route to completion, so it can deny completion despite an image that visibly fulfills the requested pencil-drawing style. The support checks otherwise distinguish progress from completion and preserve unresolved evidence appropriately.
